conversation.user: I am an international applicant interested in the Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering. Is it available to international applicants?
conversation.advisor:
Yes. The **Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering** is listed as **available to international applicants** for the full-time program.

The program’s international eligibility record is marked **“ACCEPTED_AVAILABLE.”** However, study-permit information is listed as **not published**, and availability may still depend on the specific intake and offering. Admission is competitive and includes:

- High-school graduation
- English Studies 12 (or equivalent): **73%**
- Pre-Calculus 12 (or accepted equivalent): **73%**
- Chemistry 11: **73%**
- Physics 12: **73%**
- One approved Grade 12 academic course: **73%**
- Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire
- Departmental competitive ranking

Please confirm current intake availability and study-permit requirements with the institution. [Program information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-engineering-bachelor-of-engineering-full-time-8660beng/)

For more information, see BCIT International Students: https://www.bcit.ca/international-students/.

expectation.question: I am an international applicant interested in the Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering. Is it available to international applicants?
expectation.expected: Use this program's INTERNATIONAL evidence. Distinguish available, restricted, not accepted, and unknown; never infer ineligibility from silence.

conversation.user: So does that automatically mean I'm admitted?
conversation.advisor:
No. Being **eligible to apply** or having the program listed as available to international applicants does **not automatically mean you have been admitted**.

Admission also involves meeting the stated requirements, submitting the Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire, and the program’s competitive ranking. The final ranking and admission decision require institutional confirmation.

[Program information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-engineering-bachelor-of-engineering-full-time-8660beng/)

expectation.question: So does that automatically mean I'm admitted?

conversation.user: What can you actually verify, and what should I confirm with BCIT?
conversation.advisor:
Here is what the available Asteris/BCIT program data supports for the **Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering**:

### Verified

- The program is listed as **available to international applicants** with an international status of **“ACCEPTED_AVAILABLE.”**
- The program is **full-time**, delivered **in person** at the **Burnaby campus**.
- Initial admission requirements include:
  - High-school graduation
  - **English Studies 12** or Category 1 equivalent: **73%**
  - **Pre-Calculus 12** or an accepted BC/Yukon equivalent: **73%**
  - **Chemistry 11**: **73%**
  - **Physics 12**: **73%**
  - One approved Grade 12 academic course: **73%**
  - The **Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire**
  - Competitive departmental ranking
- The program record indicates **“PGWP: ELIGIBLE_TO_APPLY.”** This is not a guarantee of a post-graduation work permit.
- The program is structured as four years of full-time academic study. Successful completion of the first two years leads to a **Civil Engineering Diploma**, subject to the program’s continuation requirements.

### Not verified from the available data

- Whether applications are currently open for your intended intake
- Whether your specific international courses or credentials are accepted as equivalents
- Whether your chosen Grade 12 academic course is on the approved list
- Whether your application is complete or has been accepted
- Your competitive ranking or admission decision
- Current study-permit requirements; the program record marks this information as **not published**
- Any application, document, acceptance, enrolment, or reapplication deadlines

### Confirm directly with BCIT

Ask BCIT Admissions or BCIT International to confirm:

1. Current international availability for your intended intake  
2. Equivalency of your English, mathematics, chemistry, physics, and other academic credentials  
3. Whether your Grade 12 academic course qualifies  
4. How and when to submit the Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire  
5. Whether you meet the competitive-admission requirements and when decisions will be issued  
6. Current study-permit guidance and any international-student documentation requirements  
7. Whether the PGWP information applies to your specific intake and circumstances  

Being eligible to apply—or seeing the program marked as available to international applicants—does **not** mean that you have been admitted.

[BCIT Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering program information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-engineering-bachelor-of-engineering-full-time-8660beng/)

programs.program_overview: The BEng in Civil Engineering is composed of four years of full-time academic study. The first two years of the degree program present a broad, practical overview of the field of civil engineering, with engineering fundamentals stressed and reinforced across the curriculum. You will receive an abundance of learning opportunities to apply these fundamentals to the solution of real-world design scenarios that would be encountered by both technologists and engineers. Throughout the program, we will present opportunities to strengthen your graphical, written, and oral communication skills. You will spend a significant amount of time on hands-on training in material testing, surveying, manual and computer-aided drafting, and receive instruction in the use of engineering software tools. You will receive a Diploma in Civil Engineering credential upon successful completion of the first two years of academic study within this degree program.  If you meet the continuation requirements, you may continue into the final two years of the degree program which are academically rigorous. We will thoroughly investigate the theoretical foundations of civil engineering science and design topics. At the same time, you will apply the practical civil engineering knowledge you have gained in course assignments and project work. You will also be challenged to view the engineer’s role from an interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary perspective. You will learn about the role of the engineer in project and construction management and enrich your educational experience with complementary studies courses relating to social sciences and the humanities. To further develop your engineering skills for professional practice, you will work with classmates to complete a team-based capstone design project.

To further develop your engineering skills for professional practice, you will work with classmates to complete a team-based capstone design project.
